{{tl|av}} is a complex template - this is a reference guide explaining some important parts.  
==Structure==
This template consists of 2 main parts: '''[[#Variables|Variable definitions]]''' and a '''[[#Table|table]]''' (as well as documentation).

===Variables===
Variables are used to cut down on <tt>#ifexist</tt> - storing the result in a variable does not require multiple, identical invocations of an expensive parser function (also, it's a lot easier to read).

The variables defined in the template are list
*<tt>PAGE</tt>: The current page - uses the first parameter to av if specified, or defaults to <nowiki>{{PAGENAME}}</nowiki> (this is not implemented completely – you can specify a page name for av to use, but the colors are still determined by the namespace)
* '''Existence checks'''
**<tt>e4</tt>, <tt>e3</tt>, <tt>e2</tt>, <tt>e1</tt>: These variables are set to 1 if the article exists in the corresponding namespace. The <tt>e</tt> stands for "exists".
*** Currently, DF2012=4, v0.31=3, 40d=2, and 23a=1. DF2012 is likely to change when the next version is released, so using the namespace as the variable name would make updating the template harder.
*** Note that this variable is '''blank''' when the page does not exist (this is for easy use with <tt>#if</tt>, which treats a blank string as false). If you need 0 to represent false, use <tt><nowiki>{{#var:e4|0}}</nowiki></tt> (this technique is used with <tt>eboth</tt>)
**<tt>emw</tt>: 1 if the page exists in the Masterwork (mod) namespace
**<tt>evan</tt> (Abbreviation of "'''e'''xists in '''van'''illa DF"): 1 if the page exists in ''any'' vanilla namespace
**<tt>emod</tt>: 1 if the page exists in any mod namespace. This is currently redundant, since Masterwork is the only mod currently implemented. However, this should '''not''' be used when checking for a mod (don't resort to <tt>emw</tt> just because it works at the moment)
**<tt>ismod</tt>: 1 if the ''current page'' is about a mod (not exactly related, but close enough)
**<tt>eboth</tt>: 1 if the page exists in a vanilla '''and''' mod namespace
**<tt>enone</tt>: 1 if the page does not exist in a vanilla or mod namespace (this is '''not''' the opposite of <tt>eboth</tt> - both are blank if the page exists in one set of namespaces but not the other)
